title: Adaptive slice-retry patterns and keepalive-priming for streaming SDKs (Python/TS/Go)
creator: Asha Patel
description: Background: Customers surface two recurring production pain points: 1) large streaming requests that error mid-flight and must be retried (causing duplicate work or user-visible truncation), and 2) intermittent cold-connection latency spikes after idle periods (especially for low-traffic routes). Goal: deliver a cross-SDK pattern for (a) adaptive request-slicing + retry semantics that minimize duplicated work for large streamed uploads/requests and (b) a lightweight keepalive-priming strategy to reduce first-byte latency after idle periods. The work must include concrete, idiomatic examples for Python, TypeScript, and Go SDKs, and an RFC-level doc for the runtime/transport teams to adopt. Scope: - Library-level examples and helpers in each SDK (not required to change server-side APIs) - Transport config presets (names and recommended default values) that map to runtime knobs (idle_reap, keepalive_probe_ms, per-route-deadline-multiplier) - Telemetry events to measure success (slice_retry_count, priming_latency_ms, prime_success)
acceptance_criteria: Docs: RFC + examples describing slice/retry semantics and priming behavior published to internal Confluence (link in links)
SDKs: Python/TS/Go include sample helper functions and a short recipe in the repo examples folder
Telemetry: demo dashboard with priming latency and slice retry rates created (link)
Perf: 50% reduction in median first-byte latency for idle connections in the low-traffic canary (measured vs baseline)
Robustness: When a slice fails, SDK retries only the minimum necessary bytes/segments and exposes idempotency hooks to callers
